class: HCN channel blocker; the authors call it a nonselective inhibitor of HCN isoforms (the label "open-channel" is in none of the cited papers and is not used)
mechanism_source: 34018186 Abstract, Results "Effect of IVA on cortical and thalamic neuron properties", Discussion ("a nonselective inhibitor of HCN channel isoforms"); Fig 5 caption
measured_in: Rat slices 25-35 days old, 35 C, K-gluconate internal, junction potential -13 mV corrected: Wistar cortical layer 5 pyramidal neurons (n=6) and GAERS thalamic VB neurons (n=10); 3 umol/L in the text and 30 umol/L in the Fig 5 legend (source discrepancy); sag reduced from about 2.65 to about 1.4 mV (cortical, -200 pA) and about 2.8 to about 1.45 mV (VB); RMP about -61.8 to -65.7 mV (cortical) and -65.3 to -67.5 mV (VB); spikes evoked by a low-threshold spike fell (cortical 2.5 to 1.0); in vivo (GAERS, 2 h after oral dosing): free brain concentration 184 +/- 67.8 nmol/L with elacridar (n=4) and 4.7 +/- 0.1 nmol/L without (n=2)
selectivity_known_and_unknown: Known: sag reduced, RMP hyperpolarised, spikes from depolarising steps, AP amplitude and threshold unchanged in the neurons tested. Unknown: isoform preference at the concentrations used, off-target actions, effect on Rin (Rin is not shown in Fig 5), effect in layer II/III pyramidal neurons, in P13-P17 tissue or in Wwox tissue
specific_limit: Oral activity only with the efflux inhibitor elacridar (a transporter inhibitor, not an HCN agent); the strongest in-vivo effect came from injection into the cortical initiation network (96 percent) against 40 percent in VB; absence-epilepsy model; the slice concentration is 16-160 times the in-vivo free level
depth: partial_fulltext_read (34018186; text and all five figure images viewed; references not read)

class: HCN channel blocker (tool, not a candidate)
mechanism_source: 24953239 Methods ("repeated in the presence of ZD7288 (20 uM)") and Results "Burst-firing in GAERS VB neurons is normalized by Ih blockade"; Table 1; Discussion; cited neocortical use in 34634460 Discussion
measured_in: Rat VB thalamic neurons P15-P20 and adult, 33-35 C, 20 umol/L: resting potential hyperpolarised by about 15-18 mV (P15-P20 about 17-18, adult about 15-16), sag 0.39-2.13 mV (from 4-6), Rin lowered by about 9-32 percent (305 to 278, 266 to 218, 230 to 156, 175 to 137 Mohm) (peak-based Rin, measured at the more negative potential, no significance mark in Fig 6d)
selectivity_known_and_unknown: Known (abstract level and earlier partial read): inhibits Na+ current in DRG neurons and recombinant Nav1.4 (22989944; IC50 numbers carried from hcn_20261107, not re-verified here); blocks T-type current extracellularly in rat CA1 pyramidal cells, concentration dependent, with a shift of steady-state inactivation (18534748, abstract only); IC50 about 100 umol/L on native T-type current in mouse spermatogenic cells and inhibits all cloned T-type channels (14575712, abstract only; a very different cell). Unknown: the T-type and Na+ block in layer II/III pyramidal neurons at the concentration an experimenter would use; effect in Wwox cells
specific_limit: Direction of the Rin effect differs between reports (Rin up in the neocortical report cited by 34634460, Rin down in 24953239 VB); a single blocker cannot assign sag to HCN; needs a second chemotype and a voltage-clamp subtraction; an extracellular block of T-type current also changes rebound

class: Kv7 opener (the abstract names KCNQ2, KCNQ3, KCNQ2/3 and KCNQ4; KCNQ5 is not in it)
mechanism_source: 11466425 Abstract: hyperpolarising shift of activation of KCNQ2/3, KCNQ2, KCNQ3 and KCNQ4 in CHO cells and native M channels in rat sympathetic neurons; hyperpolarisation and fewer spikes in unclamped neurons without change in AP configuration; no effect on KCNQ1
measured_in: CHO cells and rat superior cervical ganglion neurons in culture; concentration not read (abstract only)
selectivity_known_and_unknown: Known from the abstract: potency order KCNQ3 > KCNQ2/3 > KCNQ2 > KCNQ4, KCNQ1 not enhanced. Unknown here: effects in cortical layer II/III pyramidal neurons, other targets, concentrations, Methods
specific_limit: A lower Rin after an opener is a physical inference, not in the abstract; an opener acts in wild-type cells too, so a hyperpolarisation or Rin fall after an opener does not show a Kv7 deficit in Wwox cells; the native M-current in the Wwox neurons has never been measured; abstract only; the paper is PDF-only in PMC and the PDF route was refused
